newsitem.title: UK: Greenpeace vessels protest at Atlantic oil tests.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace vessels protest at Atlantic oil tests.

text.p: Greenpeace activists sailed inflatable boats close to an oil exploration vessel in the north Atlantic on Monday and said they stopped it surveying for U.S. oil giant Texaco.

A Greenpeace statement said the exploration by the seismic exploration vessel Pacific Horizon was illegal because the British government had failed to ensure a full environmental impact assessment had been made.
Greenpeace said the protest by 10 activists in three inflatable craft was part of its campaign against plans to open up Atlantic waters for oil exploration. There were no reported injuries.
Texaco in a statement did not make clear whether the protest had stopped the survey but said the three craft had been sailed directly into Pacific Horizon's path.
Texaco said it regretted the action 180 nautical miles east of the tiny barren Atlantic island of Rockall off the Hebridean islands.

It said the protest was unsafe, had put both activists and exploration staff at risk and had interfered with legitimate activity. The exploration complied with British environmental standards, it said.
Greeenpeace meanwhile said it was seeking to take the British Government to court this week over the Tantlic oil exploration plans.

Spokesperson Mirella Lindenfels said the government had failed to apply the European Habitats Directive when it awarded permits in the 17th offshore licensing round for oil exploration, mainly in the Rockall Trough west of the Hebrides and north of the Shetland Islands earlier this year.

In an unprecedented move back in March Greenpeace applied for all the licenses with the intention of turning the 22,000 square miles into a marine wildlife sanctuary. The bid was rejected by the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) and the licenses were granted to 14 oil companies.
If the High Court grants Greenpeace leave the case will go to court and the group said it will call for the oil exploration to be suspended until the case is concluded.
The DTI rejection of the Greenpeace license bid heralded the start of concerted campaigning.
Earlier this month activists occupied the London office of U.S. oil company Conoco, which among others was awarded the right to explore for oil in the 17th licensing round, for about four hours.
A week ago Greenpeace campaigners seized Rockall and rejecting British claims proclaimed a new state of Waveland in a gesture aimed at protecting the Atlantic Frontier from oil exploration.

The Department of Trade and Industry said the government's position had been laid out in a letter sent to Greenpeace on June 18, adding the government would go to court if it felt that was necessary to achieve its aims.
